nodes.label: The toast gate is latched by pointerdown, so fireEvent.click tests never hear the second cue
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - pin-batch-e-8-files [ses_f1769943fffeYLDactR4alJA9k].md:L5209] the toast sound is gated on `userInteracted` which is latched by `pointerdown`/`keydown`/`touchstart` capture listeners on window. In tests using `fireEvent.click`, no `pointerdown` is dispatched by default.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - pin-batch-e-8-files [ses_f1769943fffeYLDactR4alJA9k].md:L5231] in production, the user has interacted (pointerdown), so mark-complete plays click_001.ogg AND confirmation_001.ogg. That IS a double cue.
nodes.norm_label: the toast gate is latched by pointerdown so fireevent click tests never hear the second cue

nodes.label: Mark Complete double-cues in production because the button cue and the success toast cue both fire
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - pin-batch-e-8-files [ses_f1769943fffeYLDactR4alJA9k].md:L8708] The button plays `click_001.ogg`, and `handleCompleteTask` raises a success toast which `playToastSound` also cues. With the toast gate open, which is the real state in every session (the latch is flipped by the user's own pointerdown), one activation emits two sounds.
nodes.norm_label: mark complete double cues in production because the button cue and the success toast cue both fire
